scope: Correction of cross-task fallback action validation and fail-closed H3 identity delivery
summary: The earlier v19 fallback delivery is withdrawn after matched current-task evaluation exposed severe action and motion regressions. The hardened router requires complete same-task assessments and exact context hashes for both branches, then correctly blocks without emitting a video because neither branch passes.
evidence: The user rejected the earlier delivered SHA-256 d453533bc6e914f7ed09d0587b51580e44ffe7eccee4271ea5209b4801c91dac because its action differs substantially from the original/current inspect-flower trajectory.
A new decoded-frame-bound review of that exact 832x480x124 video passes visible 2-D topology in 124/124 frames, separating structural stability from action correctness.

Against the current motion-control SHA-256 23bf06de7cbbe26e9219b1a574dc4182c7a10d8c6cca78a0349ea0009bf363dd, raw motion preservation falls from 0.5700226814 to 0.1651698615 and EPL minimum falls from 0.5167504084 to 0.1439176164.
The matched automatic assessment reports motion adherence 0.4458967384 and action adherence 0.2785050851, so motion_non_regression and action_non_regression both fail.

The router now requires all 12 promotion gates and rejects legacy manifests or incomplete gate lists. Candidate and fallback metric bundles must share exact SHA-256 values for source, current action control, robot reference, anchor mask, frozen baseline, baseline action evaluation, identity mask, reference image, and scene image.
The hardened routing manifest has SHA-256 38e6d8fa206368a6e115523a1e390e37762c8c43eec23b3fe7537f5ee0238a8e, records status=blocked and output=null, and its directory contains no delivered.mp4.
Twenty-two focused identity/routing tests pass after adding the complete-gate and task-context requirements.

The local project virtual environment was unavailable because its pyvenv.cfg was a zero-block dataless file; verification was run in the existing remote .venv-h3 environment instead of modifying the user's environment.
One audit command used lora_rank=0 and was rejected by the reviewed-round validator before creating an experiment; the corrected audit used rank 8 only as schema metadata and made no training claim.

The first hardened-router invocation found that the candidate assessment had not yet been synchronized to the remote evidence tree and failed before output creation; after copying the immutable assessment, the unique v2 route completed and blocked correctly.
lessons: A fallback is not safe merely because it passed action checks in its source experiment; its exact encoded frames must be rescored against the current task control.
Topology and action are independent hard constraints. Passing one must never compensate for a catastrophic regression in the other.
Delivery contracts must bind task context by content hash and require the full canonical gate set, otherwise stale or partial evidence can be mistaken for current acceptance.
When no candidate satisfies every non-regression gate, correct behavior is to emit no demo rather than preserve the appearance of progress.
limitations: The correction makes delivery fail closed; it does not produce a new learned candidate that meets the full contract.
The v19 topology result remains a visible 2-D observation and does not prove 3-D anatomy, contact physics, or real execution.
The learned H3 capability remains PARTIAL because the structural candidate and the action-preserving fallback fail different hard gates.
next_actions: Do not deliver either the r3 candidate or the v19 fallback for the current inspect-flower task.
Require future candidates and fallbacks to pass the same complete task-bound assessment before video creation.
Resume model work only with a structural/action control mechanism capable of improving topology without reducing current-control action and motion below the 0.99 non-regression floor.
